components.name: Button
components.title: Button
components.summary: Button runs an action with a text label: Play, Follow, Remind me, Done.
components.use: an action with a word on it: the one main action of a view, the action beside it, and the confirmation in a dialog that deletes something.

instead.when: an action inside a sentence or a row of text
an action that one glyph says better than a word
narrowing what a feed shows
switching between views of the same thing
a choice whose options each need a picture or a line of explanation
signing in with Apple or Google

accessibility_declared.design: A native button (a link with `href`): Tab reaches it, Enter activates it, and Space does too on a button; `disabled` takes a button out of the tab order. A screen reader hears its text (or `aria-label`), with `trailing`'s value and its `label` read after it ("~100 fragments"); icons and the mark are hidden. With `href` and `disabled` it is drawn as a disabled button, out of the tab order, since a link cannot be disabled. With `busy` it keeps focus and its place in the tab order but is `aria-disabled`, so Enter, Space and a click do nothing; after the delay a screen reader hears `busyLabel` once (or "Save, working" without it), and `doneLabel` when it ends; a wait shorter than the delay says nothing. In forced colours it keeps an edge in ButtonText, and a disabled one turns GrayText.

components.name: ProviderButton
components.title: ProviderButton
components.summary: ProviderButton is the button for signing in with Apple or Google, in the provider's own mark and colours as each provider sets them.
components.use: signing in or creating an account with Apple or Google.

instead.when: any other action
linking an account inside the product (YouTube, a connector)

accessibility_declared.design: A native button (a link with `href`): Tab reaches it, Enter activates it, and Space does too on a button; `disabled` takes a button out of the tab order. A screen reader hears its label ("Continue with Apple"); the provider's mark is hidden. With `href` and `disabled` it is a disabled button. Under reduced motion its press does not scale, and in forced colours it keeps an edge.

components.name: IconButton
components.title: IconButton
components.summary: IconButton is a circular control holding one icon, with a required accessible `label`.
components.use: an action that one glyph says better than a word: back, share, like, captions, the bell.

instead.when: an action whose meaning needs a word
a glyph that only decorates
asking Maki

accessibility_declared.design: A button (a link with `href`): Tab reaches it, Enter activates it, and Space does too on a button; the icon is hidden. Name it with `label`; without one it has no name, and with `pressed` set it is a toggle announced "pressed" or "not pressed". A link is never a toggle: a pressed link is said to be the current one (`aria-current`) and keeps the pressed look. With `href` and `disabled` it is a disabled button. In forced colours it keeps an edge, and pressed takes Highlight.

components.name: Chip
components.title: Chip
components.summary: Chip filters a feed by kind: All, Episodes, Shorts, Manga, Following.
components.use: narrowing what a feed or a list shows, one kind at a time; with `variant="soft"`, picking several words from a set, such as traits.

instead.when: running an action
two to four views of the same thing
words the person keeps and removes
a label on artwork or a state on a surface

accessibility_declared.design: Tab focuses each chip; Enter or Space runs `onClick`. A screen reader hears the group named by Chip.Group's `label`, then each chip as a button, "pressed" when `selected` (a `removable` one is a plain button, "Remove Smith"); the icon is hidden. When a keyed chip leaves the group with focus on it, focus goes to the chip now in its place, else the last one. In forced colours each chip keeps an edge, and a selected one takes Highlight. A soft chip is a 44px target, though it draws at 32px.

components.name: SegmentedControl
components.title: SegmentedControl
components.summary: SegmentedControl switches between two to four views of the same thing: series sections, Following / For you, reading direction.
components.use: switching between two to four views of the same thing (series sections, Following and For you), or a setting with two to four named values.

instead.when: five options or more
one setting that is on or off
narrowing a feed by kind
going to another part of the product

reviewed.reason: The selected label sits on the sliding highlight, a separate element the checker can't see. Measured on screen it is about 19:1 in both themes.

accessibility_declared.design: Tab focuses each option; Enter or Space picks it. A screen reader hears the group's `label`, then each option as a button, "pressed" when selected. Dragging the pill is for the pointer; Enter or Space on an option does the same.

components.name: OptionTiles
components.title: OptionTiles
components.summary: OptionTiles is the Studio's picker: a grid of tiles, each an AniCanon icon over a short name, for shot type, angle, depth, movement, mood, lighting, weather, effects and frame format.
components.use: a choice that is clearer seen than read: Studio's direction pickers (shot, angle, lighting) as tiles, and with `size="lg"` the first choice of a flow, a pack or a plan as cards.

instead.when: a short list of plain words
two to four views of the same thing
one setting on or off
one thing among many, with pictures and search

accessibility_declared.design: Ways in (options with `href`) are a group named by `label`, each tile a link (a button with `onClick` alone) read as its name and description. With one choice the tiles are a radio group: one Tab stop, on the chosen tile (the first when none is), so a Dialog opens on the chosen tile; the arrows move to a tile and choose it, Home and End go to the first and last, and an option's `disabled` is skipped. With `multiple` each tile is a toggle button: Tab focuses each one, and Enter or Space picks it. A screen reader hears the group, named by the words of `label` (or `ariaLabel`), then each tile with its name, as a radio ("checked" when chosen) or with `multiple` a toggle button ("pressed"), large tiles adding the badge, the amount or cost with its label ("24,990 fragments"), the description and the footnote, with icons and art hidden.

components.name: Switch
components.title: Switch
components.summary: Switch turns one thing on or off, with its name as the `label` (the visible text sits beside it).
components.use: one setting that takes effect the moment it changes: Loop this track, Name who speaks.

instead.when: a choice between named options
a value on a range
choosing things to act on together, or agreeing to terms

accessibility_declared.design: A switch named by `label` that Tab reaches; Enter or Space flips it through `onChange`, it is announced "on" or "off", and `disabled` takes it out of the tab order. With `showLabel` the whole row is its label, so a click on the text flips it too, and the `hint` is its description. Sliding the knob is for the pointer; Enter or Space does the same. In forced colours the track draws an edge and the knob a solid in the system colours (Highlight when on), and the switch keeps its size.

components.name: PanelRow
components.title: PanelRow
components.summary: PanelRow is Studio’s folded section: an icon, the section’s name and its current value, with the chevron that opens it, at the row's end with or without a value.
components.use: a folded Studio section: its icon, its name and what it is set to (Close-up · push in · low), with the chevron that opens it.

instead.when: several kinds of setting listed together, each opening its full choice
a Studio card with its controls showing
one thing on a row of a list
one setting on or off

accessibility_declared.design: A button (a link with `href`) that Tab reaches; Enter runs `onClick`, and Space does too on a button. A screen reader hears its title and value, then, when `open` is given on a button, expanded or collapsed from it; the icon and chevron are hidden.

components.name: TextLink
components.title: TextLink
components.summary: TextLink is a quiet action inside a line or a row of text: Accept, Decline, Why; Ask Maki; Use it.
components.use: a quiet action beside what it acts on, inside a line or a row of text (Accept, Decline, Why), and the way into a deletion.

instead.when: the action a view exists for
an action shown as a glyph alone
a row that opens a page

accessibility_declared.design: A link with `href`, otherwise a button: Tab reaches it, Enter activates it (Space too as a button), and a screen reader hears its text or `aria-label`, with the icon hidden. `variant` changes only its look. For a link that opens a dialog, `aria-haspopup`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pass through. Its underline at rest tells it apart from the text around it without colour (WCAG 1.4.1).

components.name: TextField
components.title: TextField
components.summary: A labelled text input or text area.
components.use: words a person types, on one line or in a text area: a name, a description, a search.

instead.when: one choice from a list
a number stepped a unit at a time
words kept as separate tags
Studio's prompt, with who and where it binds
writing to Maki

accessibility_declared.design: A text input (a text area with `multiline`) that Tab reaches and that takes typing, named by the words of `label` (with "optional"), or by `placeholder` without one, and described by `hint`; `required` adds "required", and `readOnly` makes it read-only. `onChange` gets the text as it is typed. The icon is hidden.

components.name: SearchField
components.title: SearchField
components.summary: A search: TextField's box with the search icon, a clear button once there are words, and, when the page passes `results`, Picker's options under it.
components.use: finding something by its words: in a series, the library, all of AniCanon.

instead.when: choosing one thing for a field (a cast member for a shot)
filtering a list already on screen by a few known values
writing to Maki

accessibility_declared.design: A search landmark named by `label`, holding a search field of the same name that Tab reaches. Enter submits the words, or chooses the active result; Escape closes the results, then clears the words, then calls `onClose`. With `results` the field is a combobox: Up and Down move its active descendant through the options (Up or Down opens closed results), each option reads as Picker's do, and one status line says how many results there are, that it is searching, or `emptyText`. The clear button is "Clear search" and gives focus back to the field. The icon is hidden.

components.name: Select
components.title: Select
components.summary: A labelled single-choice control that opens a list.
components.use: one choice from a short list of plain values, in a labelled field that opens the list: a faction, with its icon.

instead.when: one thing among many, with search and groups
two to four named values seen at once
a choice that is clearer seen than read
a colour chosen by eye

accessibility_declared.design: A select-only combobox named by the words of `label` together with its value ("Faction Heros"), else by `placeholder`, and described by `hint`; Tab reaches it, and focus stays on it while its list is open. Down, Up, Enter or Space open the list, the arrows, Home, End and a first letter move the active option (read as the active descendant, "selected" on the chosen one), Enter or Space picks it, and Escape or Tab closes the list. The arrows still reach a `disabled` option, read as unavailable with its reason after its label, and it can't be picked. The active option is kept in view, and with no `options` the field is unavailable. When the page changes `value` the name follows it, and a `value` not among the options is named by the placeholder, never by its key, with no option read as selected.

components.name: Checkbox
components.title: Checkbox
components.summary: Checkbox is one thing chosen or not, among others that may be chosen too: the files to queue, the rows to delete, the terms you agree to.
components.use: choosing any number of things at once, or for one agreement: rows for a bulk action, files to queue, "I agree to the terms".

instead.when: a setting that takes effect the moment it changes
choosing among options drawn as tiles
choosing one thing among many, with pictures and search

accessibility_declared.design: A checkbox named by `label` that Tab reaches; Enter or Space flips it through `onChange`, and it is announced "checked", "not checked" or "mixed". `disabled` takes it out of the tab order. With `showLabel` the row is its label, so a click on the words flips it too, and the `hint` is its description. The mark is hidden; the state is said. In forced colours the edge and the mark draw in the system colours.

components.name: DropZone
components.title: DropZone
components.summary: Where a file goes: drop or choose.
components.use: where a file goes, dropped or chosen, then read and held: a clip to bring in.

instead.when: a page or a list with nothing in it yet
a frame waiting for a picture that will be made
choosing one thing already in the story, such as a place

accessibility_declared.design: A button that Tab reaches, named by its `title` and `hint` (and "added" once filled), with the icon hidden; filled with an `image` it is a group named by `title`, its picture's alt is `alt`, and its Remove is a button of its own; while busy it carries aria-busy, says its title and hint once through the page's live region as it starts, and its loader stays quiet. With `onFiles`, Enter, Space or a click open the file chooser (after `onClick`, which can prevent it) and a drop hands the files over.

components.name: FieldHelp
components.title: FieldHelp
components.summary: FieldHelp is the ⓘ beside a field name.
components.use: the ⓘ beside a field's name that says what the field controls, in one bold line and examples: shot type, depth of field. With `examples`, for showing each case of a choice with its picture: how much a thing matters in a shot.

instead.when: context everyone should see, kept on the page
a hover card on a mention or a small form
an action shown as a glyph alone

accessibility_declared.design: A button that Tab reaches, announced "About" plus `label` (or "About this field") and described by its tip. Focus or hover shows the tip, and the tip can be hovered without closing. Escape hides it, whether focus or the pointer opened it, until focus or the pointer leaves. The button is a 24px target, though it draws at 20px. With `examples` it is a button with `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`; a press opens a dialog named by `title` that takes focus, and Escape, a press outside or the done button closes it and returns focus to the ⓘ; with `dialog` it is a modal Dialog that keeps focus inside.

components.name: SwatchPicker
components.title: SwatchPicker
components.summary: SwatchPicker chooses a colour by eye: round swatches, the chosen one ringed.
components.use: a colour chosen by eye from round swatches: a skin tone, a creature's coat (Tabby, Calico).

instead.when: a choice that reads best as an icon over a name
a short list of plain words
any colour, typed or picked from the whole range (a brand colour)
adjusting colour in the editor

accessibility_declared.design: A radio group named by `label` and one Tab stop: arrows move to a swatch and choose it, each a radio named by its option's label and "checked" when chosen. The visible names and pattern drawings are hidden.

components.name: ColorPicker
components.title: ColorPicker
components.summary: ColorPicker chooses any colour: a field for saturation and brightness, a hue track and the hex.
components.use: when the colour can be any colour: a brand colour, a design's own colour.

instead.when: a colour chosen from a fixed set (skin, coat)
adjusting colour in the editor

accessibility_declared.design: A group named by `label`. The field is a slider named "Saturation and brightness" that speaks both; arrows move it 1% (10% with Shift), left and right for saturation, up and down for brightness. The hue track is a slider named "Hue" in degrees: arrows by 1 (10 with Shift), Page Up and Page Down by 30, Home and End. The hex field is a text field named by `label` and "hex". Presets and picture colours are radio groups (see SwatchPicker), the chosen one checked when it matches.

components.name: DateField
components.title: DateField
components.summary: DateField picks a date, or a range of dates read by period: this month, the quarter, the dates on an invoice.
components.use: a date or a span of dates someone picks or reads by period.

instead.when: a choice from a few named periods only
a time of day or a duration

accessibility_declared.design: The field is a button named by `label` and the dates, that opens a dialog named by `label`. Each month is a grid named by its month and year, with one Tab stop: arrows move a day or a week, Page Up and Page Down a month (with Shift a year), Home and End to the start and end of the week, and Enter or Space picks. Days in the range are selected, days out of reach disabled, and today is the current date; the new month is announced when it changes. The presets are a listbox with one Tab stop. Escape, a press outside or Tab out of it closes, and after Escape focus goes back to the field. Sliding across days is for the pointer; two presses, or the keys, do the same.

components.name: Field
components.title: Field
components.summary: Field puts the form's label over a control that does not carry its own (a segmented control, chips, a group of options), with an optional hint under it.
components.use: the label and hint over a control that has none of its own: a segmented control, chips, a group of options, swatches.

instead.when: typed words, which carry their own label
a list choice, which carries its own label
explaining a field on hover or focus
a label over a strip or a group inside a panel

reviewed.reason: The flagged label is a SegmentedControl's selected segment, on its sliding highlight, which the checker can't see. Measured on screen it is about 19:1 in both themes.

accessibility_declared.design: A group named by its `label` and described by its `hint`, so the control inside is announced within it, with "optional" read as part of the name.

components.name: SliderRow
components.title: SliderRow
components.summary: SliderRow is a labelled value on a track: the name, the track (0–100) and the readout as the creator reads it (`+0.2`, `−3 dB`, `100%`).
components.use: a value set by feel on a track, with its readout in the unit people use: colour, volume, opacity and loudness in the editor.

instead.when: a value where one unit matters, such as 1px or 2°
a sound's level with its mute
one setting on or off
the playhead of an episode or a short

accessibility_declared.design: A slider named by `label` that Tab reaches, its value spoken as the `readout` (the name and readout beside it are hidden, so neither is read twice); with `onChange`, arrows move it by 1 (10 with Shift), Page Up and Page Down by 10, and Home and End to 0 and 100. Without `onChange` it reads as read-only, and `disabled` takes it out of the tab order and marks it disabled.

components.name: NumberField
components.title: NumberField
components.summary: NumberField is a number you type or step a unit at a time: its name, a step down, the value with its unit, a step up.
components.use: a number where one unit matters, typed or stepped a unit at a time: a 1px border, 2° of rotation, a font size.

instead.when: a feel such as strength or mix, where the readout is the point
nudging a cut's in or out a frame at a time
words

accessibility_declared.design: A spinbutton named by `label` that takes typing, handed over on Enter or leaving it: Up and Down step it through `onStep` and its value is read with its unit, and `min` and `max` give its range. Tab also reaches the "Less" and "More" buttons on either side ("More duration"), whose steps are said aloud.

components.name: TopNav
components.title: TopNav
components.summary: TopNav is the desktop header: the AniCanon mark and wordmark, the main sections as text links, and search and account on the right.
components.use: the desktop header: the AniCanon mark, up to five main sections (Home, Series, Shorts, Manga, Creators), search and the account.

instead.when: navigation on a phone
the creator's workspace sections
the views inside a production
the top bar of a full-screen flow

accessibility_declared.design: A header whose brand link reads the name (the logo is hidden; without `brand.href` the brand is the name alone, not a link), then a navigation named by `label` (default "Main") whose links mark the current page (a link without `href` is a button running its `onClick`, never a link to #); Tab moves through them, then the `actions`, then, when there is an account or Create, "Search" (running `onSearch`, or `search.onOpen`; while searching, the search landmark and "Close search" take the links' place and Search is gone), then Create and the account button ("Your account, Aiko Mori", running `account.onClick`).

components.name: SideNav
components.title: SideNav
components.summary: The creator sidebar: product, a switcher for the current workspace, grouped sections, a footer slot and the signed-in account at the bottom.
components.use: the creator sidebar: the switcher for the current workspace, grouped sections and the signed-in account at the bottom.

instead.when: the main sections a viewer moves between on desktop
the views and scenes inside a production
navigation on a phone
the rail inside a production

accessibility_declared.design: A complementary region named by `label` (default "Sections"); Tab moves through the brand link (without `brand.href`, the name alone), the fold button, the series switcher ("Series: Ember Bay. Switch", expanded or collapsed from `switcher.open`, running `switcher.onClick`, controlling `switcher.controls`), the links of a navigation named "Sections navigation" (each group named by its title, the current link "current page"; an item without `href` is a button running its `onClick`), the footer slot (`children`) and the account button ("Your account, Aiko Mori", running `account.onClick`). Icons and pictures are hidden. The fold button is named for what it does next ("Show icons only", "Show the full menu"). Folded, every name stays for a screen reader and the tip shows it on focus. Compact keeps every name: the switcher and the account are named as above, each item by its name under its icon, and the group titles stay as the groups' names.

components.name: TabBar
components.title: TabBar
components.summary: TabBar is the phone's main navigation: a floating glass capsule with four destinations and a separate round Create button.
components.use: the phone's main navigation: four destinations (Home, Shorts, Manga, You) and the separate Create button.

instead.when: navigation on desktop
switching between views of the same thing
choices that belong to the current screen

accessibility_declared.design: A navigation named by `label` (default "Tabs"): Tab moves through each destination, a link read by its text with the current one marked "current page", then the round Create button, named by `createLabel` (default "Create"). In the web form Create is the fifth link, marked "current page" when `createCurrent`. An item with no address is a button. Icons are hidden.

components.name: PageHeader
components.title: PageHeader
components.summary: PageHeader opens an app page: its `title`, the `lead` under it that says what the page holds, and at the end the page's view switch (`slot="views"`) and its one primary action (`slot="action"`).
components.use: the top of an app page beside the SideNav (Characters, Places, Library, Series settings, You, Create): its title, its lead, and its view switch and main action.

instead.when: opening a shelf or a section inside a page
the top of a production view, with its eyebrow and Maki
the top bar of a full-screen flow
the head of a side panel or an inspector

accessibility_declared.design: A header landmark whose title is a level-1 heading (`as` changes the level), read before the lead as text; Tab reaches the view switch, then the action. Below 768 px the action sits on the title's line while the switch follows the lead, so the order read and tabbed is title, lead, switch, action.

components.name: SectionHeader
components.title: SectionHeader
components.summary: SectionHeader opens a shelf: a heading, the line that explains what is on it, and an optional See all link.
components.use: the heading that opens a shelf, with the line that says what is on it ("Shorts · videos under a minute") and an optional See all link.

instead.when: a labelled group of rows in a Story panel, with its count
the top of a side panel in Story
the top of an app page, with its title-1 and view switch
the top of a production view
the label over a single control in a form

accessibility_declared.design: The title is a heading (`as`, default h2) with its count read inside it, then the subtitle as text, and Tab reaches the See all link, named by `action.ariaLabel` or `action.label` (an action with only `onClick` is a button, never a link to #); the icon is hidden. At size xs the title is plain text, not a heading, with its count and subtitle read after it.

components.name: Pagination
components.title: Pagination
components.summary: Pagination reads a long list a page at a time: what this page holds, then previous, the page numbers and next.
components.use: reading a long list a page at a time, under the list it pages: productions at 24 a page, counted as "1–24 of 31 shorts".

instead.when: where a person is in a flow they step through
a shelf that leads to everything on it
the pages of a manga issue in the editor

accessibility_declared.design: A navigation region named by `label` (default "Pages"): the count reads as text, then Tab moves through "Previous page", each "Page 3" (the current one marked "current page") and "Next page", which are disabled at the ends: an arrow that turns off under focus hands focus to the current page. The ellipsis is hidden. Sliding is for the pointer; each page is still its own link or button.

components.name: FlowHeader
components.title: FlowHeader
components.summary: FlowHeader is the full-screen flow's top bar: close (nothing is kept), what is being made and for what, the steps when there are several, then what sits at the end.
components.use: the top bar of a full-screen flow: close, what is being made and for what ("New issue · Bad Memories"), the steps when there are several, and the balance.

instead.when: Back and the step's action
the desktop header of the app
the top of a production view
the editor's top bar

accessibility_declared.design: A header element: Tab reaches the close button (named by `closeLabel`, default "Close"; a link with `closeHref`) and then whatever sits at the end. The title and context are a level-1 heading, and the steps are a list named by `stepsLabel` (default "Steps") with the current one marked "current step".

components.name: FlowFooter
components.title: FlowFooter
components.summary: FlowFooter closes a step of the full-screen flow, inline under its content, or, where the step's body scrolls (New template, Edit template), placed by the flow under that body, outside the scroll, so it stays in view with the header above; the flow's layout does that, and FlowFooter itself is never sticky: Back on the left when a step precedes, then the note and the action on the right.
components.use: the foot of a step in a full-screen flow: Back when a step precedes, a note on what happens next or what it costs, then the one primary action.

instead.when: the way out of the flow
facts at the foot of a working surface

accessibility_declared.design: A footer element: Tab reaches Back (a link with `back.href`, otherwise a button running `back.onClick`) and then the actions; the note reads as text between them and the back icon is hidden.

components.name: Stepper
components.title: Stepper
components.summary: Where a person is in a short multi-step flow: done steps get a check, the current one fills.
components.use: where a person is in a short flow of three to five steps, in the top bar of a full-screen flow; `variant="bar"` on a phone.

instead.when: moving between the pages of a list
a job's stages while it runs, with the time each took
how far something being made has come
what a character is ready with

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable; an ordered list named by `label` (default "Steps"), each step read as its number and name, a done one as "Done:" and its name, and the current one marked "current step". With `variant` "bar" it is a progress bar named like "Step 2 of 4: Cast".

components.name: MediaCard
components.title: MediaCard
components.summary: MediaCard shows one episode, short or manga issue: its artwork at its real shape, then a title and a metadata line.
components.use: one episode, short or manga issue: its art at its real shape (16:9, 9:16 or a manga page), its title and a metadata line.

instead.when: a picture in a frame, such as a take or a library item
an episode or an issue announced but not out yet
a page of an issue in the editor
a cast member on the cast page

accessibility_declared.design: With `href` it is a link that Tab reaches and Enter follows, named by `label` if given, else by its content in order (any artwork and logo alt text, badge, duration, count, title, meta) ending with "waiting for you" when `attention` is set and "watched 40%" from `progress`; without `href` the same reads as text. The artwork's alt is `alt` and the logo's `logoAlt` (both empty by default), and the spine, scrim, light and progress bar are hidden. With no `image`, the well's words are read with the card. With `menu`, its ⋯ is a button after the link, named "More for" and the title, with a menu popup: Tab reaches it after the card.

components.name: Badge
components.title: Badge
components.summary: Badge is a small label laid over artwork: a duration, a view count, or New.
components.use: a small label over artwork (a duration, a view count, New) and, on a surface, a state such as rendering or one that waits for you.

instead.when: narrowing a feed by kind
words the person keeps and removes
a state that changed, before and after
the unread mark on the bell

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable; its text is read in place. The dot and the icon are hidden, and `variant` changes only its colour. In forced colours every badge keeps an edge, and its dot stays visible.

components.name: CastAvatar
components.title: CastAvatar

the character as a whole
choosing who wears a look

components.name: CastGrid

episodes, shorts or issues in a grid

what one character is ready with
each cast member's state and next step

who a character is
wardrobe across the whole cast

components.name: VoiceTiles

choosing among sound options in the cut
a direction choice drawn as icons

components.name: PlaceCard

components.name: PanelHeader

opening a shelf or labelling a strip
a labelled group of rows with its count
a Studio card with its controls
the editor's top bar with its timecode

components.name: PanelSection
components.title: PanelSection

a group outside Story, such as a faction in a list
Studio's folded section with its current value
rows outside Story that open pages

components.name: EntityRow
components.title: EntityRow

instead.when: a row outside Story, such as a take or a setting
an open question with its planted, raised and answered steps
something found in writing, waiting for the person
the people in a character's life beside their name

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable; the name, "not at this moment" when `faded`, its source, its state and the chip read as text in order, then whatever sits at the end. Pictures and initials are hidden, and a faded row dims its picture while its words stay readable.

components.name: StateChange
components.title: StateChange

components.use: a change written as before and after, two badges with the before faded: a place that starts burning, a bond that turns to rivals.

instead.when: a single state laid over artwork
a proposed change to words
the change as a whole row with its picture

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable; read as "Changed from", the before badge, "to" and the after badge, with the arrow itself hidden, and with no `before` it reads the after badge alone.

components.name: EventGlyph
components.title: EventGlyph
components.summary: EventGlyph is the mark of an event type, the same everywhere a story event appears: map, scrubber, rows, mentions, pickers.
components.use: the mark of a story event's type wherever one appears (map, scrubber, rows, mentions, pickers): event, twist, revelation, clue or goal.

instead.when: a glyph from the outline set
an event as a row with its state

accessibility_declared.design: Decorative: hidden from screen readers, so the event type it draws is not announced.

components.name: StoryMap
components.title: StoryMap
components.summary: StoryMap draws the story on a canvas you move: characters (portraits) and places (art) are hubs; events are small shapes, linked to the hubs they involve.
components.use: the story drawn as hubs and events on a canvas: characters and places as hubs, events on a thread in story order, and a selection's causes and conflicts.

instead.when: moving through the story in story order
the same characters, places and events as rows in a panel
the open questions the audience waits on

accessibility_declared.design: A group named by `label` (default "Story map: characters and places as hubs, events between them") whose hubs and events are one Tab stop the arrows move through, each read with what the drawing shows (an event's type, "proposed", "new", "not at this moment", "not placed", "current" on the focus) and, when `interactive`, as "movable". Dragging has a keyboard way: Shift and an arrow moves the hub or event in focus, and + and − zoom. With `onSelect` each is a button. Tab then reaches the held labels ("Show Mio"), the chip ("Remove" and its words), then the controls in the order drawn: "Zoom in", "Zoom out", "Fit the map" and "Key", which says whether the key is expanded. The overview is a picture named "The whole map, with the part in view framed"; the arrows and Fit reach everything it does. A dimmed, ghost or muted node fades only its picture or shape; its name and quiet line keep their contrast.

components.name: StoryScrubber
components.title: StoryScrubber
components.summary: StoryScrubber moves through the story in story order (when things happen in the world, not when they were released).
components.use: moving through the story in story order, when things happen in the world: a column per event under arc brackets, and a handle that names the moment ("After Fire at Sé").

instead.when: the playhead of an episode or a short
the whole cut at a glance
the cut's tracks in time
the story's people, places and events as a map

accessibility_declared.design: A slider that Tab reaches, named "Show the world at a moment in the story" and read as `valueText` (else the first handle's label, else "After event 3 of 12"); with `onChange` arrows move it an event, Page Up and Page Down a tenth of the story and Home and End to either end, and without it it reads as read-only. Beside it, screen readers get the events in story order (type, title, the events at the same time, by each mark's `label` when it has one, "in the moment shown") and the arcs as lists, and, on a long story, buttons around it in the order drawn: "Earlier events" before it, then a held label ("Show Now") and "Later events" after it, each only while there is something that way; below it a group named "Show events told by" holds filter buttons that read "pressed" on the current one and run `onFilter`.

components.name: QuestionRow
components.title: QuestionRow
components.summary: QuestionRow is one open question the audience is waiting on: planted → raised → answered, each step a real event with its place.
components.use: one open question the audience is waiting on, from planted to raised to answered, each step a real event with its place.

instead.when: a character, place or event on Story
a conflict found in writing
where a person is in a flow they step through

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable; read in order as the question in quotes (then "selected" when `selected`), its badge (Waiting, Quiet or Answered) and note, then "Planted", "Raised" and "Answered" with each step's event and where it was told ("Smoke, told in Episode 1"), "Not raised yet" or "Answer it"; pictures and arrows are hidden.

components.name: MakiPanel
components.title: MakiPanel
components.summary: MakiPanel is Maki in a side area: a `SidePanel` with Maki's face and name, what is waiting, and close; the conversation; the composer at the foot.

instead.when: the button that opens it
a side area about a character, place or event
one thing Maki says

reviewed.reason: The flagged label is a SegmentedControl's selected segment, on its sliding highlight, which the checker can't see. Measured on screen it is about 19:1 in both themes.

accessibility_declared.design: A section named "Maki". Tab moves through "{count} to look at", "Close Maki", the conversation's controls and the composer; Maki's face is hidden. The conversation is a log named "Conversation with Maki", so each reply is read as it arrives, held back while `busy` or `writing`.

components.name: MakiTurn
components.title: MakiTurn
components.summary: MakiTurn is one reply from Maki: her words on the panel's edge, in `text-body-lg`, with no who-line and no box (the head already says who).
components.use: one reply from Maki in the chat, whatever it holds.

instead.when: what the person said
something Maki proposes inside the reply
one thing Review found

components.use: the person's own message in a chat with Maki.

where the person writes the next message

one thing Review found

a correction pinned to work on a sheet

components.name: MakiComposer
components.title: MakiComposer

a plain text field in a form
a message already sent

components.name: AskMaki
components.title: AskMaki
components.summary: AskMaki is Maki's one button: Maki's face and a label.

instead.when: an action that is not about Maki
a quiet Ask Maki inside a line or a row of text
Maki's column with the conversation

components.name: CutSheet
components.title: CutSheet

instead.when: the cut's tracks in time
what gets generated for one cut, on a frame grid
one row of the sheet
a plain list of things with a title and a quiet line
the script as it is written

components.name: CutRow
components.title: CutRow

instead.when: a row outside a sheet
the cut number and its approval
a row on Story

A `selected` or `changed` row starts its first cell with "Selected" or "changed", said but not shown.

a state on a surface
a whole row of the sheet

components.use: camera and timing notation as an ekonte writes it: shot size, angle, move and when it starts and stops (C.U · low · T.U 0+00 → 5+00).

instead.when: choosing a shot, an angle or a move
the direction set on a panel, a row per kind

a cut's number and approval

components.title: Revision

the Director's note on a cut
something Maki proposes inside the chat
an event or link found in writing

instead.when: one line of context inside a page
a proposed change in the words themselves
something Maki proposes inside the chat
a confirmation that something finished

components.title: Timesheet

components.use: what gets generated for a cut, on a frame grid: each video's bracket, the key frames it starts and ends on, and one line per video.

instead.when: the cut's tracks under the preview
the whole cut at a glance
camera and timing notation in a line
a cut's in and out frames while trimming

components.name: ScreenplayLine
components.title: ScreenplayLine

components.use: one block of a screenplay inside a section of the script: a slugline, action, a cue with its extension (O.S.), a parenthetical, dialogue or a transition.

instead.when: a planned line with its delivery and translation
a subtitle over video

components.use: a planned line: the speaker, the delivery, where it falls in the beat, the line in its spoken language and its translation.

instead.when: dialogue as written in the screenplay
a subtitle over video
hearing the line

components.use: the whole cut at a glance: its sections in planned proportion, the window the Timeline shows, the playhead and numbered notes from screening.

instead.when: the cut's tracks to edit
the playhead of an episode or a short being watched
how far something being made has come
moving through the story in story order

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable without `onSeek`; a group named by `label` (default "The whole cut") whose section labels (with "partly cut" or "missing"), mark labels (with "done"), the window ("Timeline shows 0:30 to 1:00"), the playhead ("Playhead at 0:42") and the total read as text. components.name: ProductionNav
components.title: ProductionNav
components.summary: ProductionNav is the side bar inside a production (an episode, a short, and later a manga issue).
components.use: the side bar inside a production (an episode, a short, a manga issue): its views, scenes and the facts that matter while making it, folding to a rail of views and tools in the editor.

instead.when: the creator sidebar outside a production, wide or `compact`
the top of a view with its title and actions
the steps of a full-screen flow
the desktop header across the app

accessibility_declared.design: A complementary region named by `label` (default "Production"): Tab moves through Back, the links of a navigation named "Views" (the current one "current page", with its note; a `disabled` view is a disabled link, out of the tab order, still read with its note: "Plan, After the script, dimmed"), the scene links ("current" on the selected one) and the balance link, while the production's title is a level-2 heading, the scenes' title a level-3 one, and each fact reads its value and percent. Collapsed, the rail's links are named by their titles ("Cast · 3 waiting"), a `disabled` one the same way and out of the tab order, the tools sit in a navigation named "Tools" and are named by their `label` (not the short word under them), and the balance is the mark alone, still a link named "Fragments balance: 1,240"; pictures, icons and the attention dot are hidden. With `production.menu`, the ⋯ is a button after the production's heading, named "More for" and the title, with a menu popup.

components.name: ViewHeader
components.title: ViewHeader
components.summary: ViewHeader opens a production view: which view it is, its title and its meta, with the view's actions on the right.
components.use: the top of a production view: the view as an eyebrow, the title on one line, the meta under it, and the view's actions on the right (Maki, then at most one primary).

instead.when: the top of an app page beside the SideNav
opening a shelf
the head of a side panel or an inspector
the editor's top bar with its timecode
the top bar of a full-screen flow

accessibility_declared.design: The title is a level-1 heading, with the eyebrow before it and the meta after it read as text; the actions on the right take focus in order.

components.name: EditorShell
components.title: EditorShell
components.summary: EditorShell is the full-screen editor (Cut).
components.use: the full-screen editor (Cut, and Art and Lettering in manga): the rail, header, tool panel, inspector and the centre column with the monitor, program bar and timeline, with `focus` for the canvas alone.

instead.when: a production view outside the editor
a full-screen flow that makes one thing step by step
a task over the page

accessibility_declared.design: A layout with no keyboard handling of its own: Tab moves through its slots in order (nav, header, tool, the tool's resize handle, centre, the inspector's resize handle, inspector); each handle is a vertical separator named "Resize the tool panel" or "Resize the inspector", its value always the pane's width as laid out, its least and most the pane's min and max, the inspector is a complementary region named by `inspectorLabel` (default "Inspector"), and EditorHeader's title is a level-1 heading. CanvasStage's selection is a group named by `label` and described by its position and size; with `onBox` it is an application (a "movable item") and one Tab stop where arrows move it and Shift with an arrow resizes it, each change said aloud, and its handles are hidden.

components.name: EditorHeader
components.title: EditorHeader
components.summary: EditorHeader is the editor's top bar: what is being edited, its timecode, whether it rebuilds exactly, and the editor's actions.
components.use: in `EditorShell`'s `header` slot.

instead.when: a production view outside the editor
a full-screen flow that makes one thing step by step

components.name: Monitor
components.title: Monitor

components.use: in `EditorShell`'s centre column for the picture being edited.

instead.when: a take shown in a list or a strip
a clip that plays where it is shown

With `picks` the picture is for the pointer: the outline and its name are hidden from assistive technology, and the timeline is where a keyboard selects the same items.

components.name: MonitorBar
components.title: MonitorBar
components.summary: MonitorBar is the bar under the editor's picture: the transport, the timecode, the edit buttons and what sits at the end.
components.use: under `Monitor` or `CanvasStage` in `EditorShell`.

instead.when: a bar of tools that floats over the canvas
the status line at the bottom of a view

accessibility_declared.design: A row with no role of its own: its buttons are in order (transport, edit buttons, end), the timecode is read as text and the separator is hidden.

components.name: CanvasStage
components.title: CanvasStage
components.summary: CanvasStage is the editor's canvas while an item on it is selected: the frame, the item at its size and place, and a box with eight handles to move and resize it.
components.use: in place of `Monitor` while an item is selected on the canvas.

instead.when: the picture while nothing is selected
a page's frames and selection in manga

accessibility_declared.design: The selection is a group named by `label` (default "Selected item") and described by its position and size. With `onBox` it is an application (a "movable item"), so a screen reader in browse mode hands it the arrows, and one Tab stop: arrows move it a percent and Shift with an arrow resizes it from its right or bottom edge, each change said aloud. The handles are for the pointer, dragged to resize, and are hidden; dragging the box moves it as the arrows do. With `onPick`, Escape on the selected box clears the selection; a click on the box that was not a drag takes the pick beneath it, and a click on its dimmed part past the frame does nothing.

components.name: TrimFrames
components.title: TrimFrames
components.summary: TrimFrames shows a cut’s in and out frames with their timecodes and a frame-at-a-time nudge under each.
components.use: the selected cut's in and out frames with their timecodes and a frame-at-a-time nudge under each, ringing the one being trimmed.

instead.when: trimming an item on the tracks by its ends
a picture in a frame
a number stepped a unit at a time
the frame grid of what gets generated for a cut

accessibility_declared.design: A group named by `label` (default "Trim"): each frame reads "In" or "Out" and its timecode, a frame with `href` is a link named like "In frame, 0:12" (with "selected" on the `active` one), and Tab reaches its nudge buttons ("In a frame earlier", "In a frame later", and the same for Out). Without `href` the nudges run `onNudge`.

components.name: VolumeControl
components.title: VolumeControl
components.summary: VolumeControl is a sound’s mute button, its level and the readout (Muted when muted).
components.use: a sound's mute button, its level and the readout (Muted when muted), such as the video's own sound on the selected cut.

instead.when: any other labelled value on a track
one setting on or off
hearing a voice line or a take

accessibility_declared.design: Tab reaches the mute button, a toggle named "Mute" plus `what` (default "the sound") and "pressed" when muted, then a slider named "Volume of the sound" and spoken as its percent or "Muted"; with `onChange`, arrows move it by 1 (10 with Shift), Page Up and Page Down by 10, and Home and End to 0 and 100. Without `onChange` the slider reads as read-only.

components.name: PromptComposer
components.title: PromptComposer
components.summary: PromptComposer is Studio's prompt: who and where it binds on top, the words, then its tools.
components.use: the prompt that makes a take (in Studio, and for episodes in Quick mode): the cast, places and references it binds on top, the words, then its tools with Generate and its cost, `variant="media"` as the phone app's dock over the take and `variant="web"` as the phone browser's.

instead.when: writing to Maki
a plain text field
the script itself
choosing direction as tiles

accessibility_declared.design: A region named by `label` (default "Prompt"): Tab reaches the refs, then the words, then the tools. A missing mention reads as its name then "missing" ("$platform-edge, missing"), and a grouped $ list is one listbox whose groups are named by their headings, the arrows moving through every group in order. With `onChange` the words are a multi-line textbox named by `promptLabel` (default "Prompt"), with `placeholder` as its placeholder: focus stays in the words while the list is open (the field controls it, `aria-autocomplete="list"`), the arrows move its active option (announced as the field's active descendant), Enter or Tab chooses it and Escape closes it; Right opens a place's views, the list then named by the place, and Left or Backspace after the # goes back, as does the head's Back button ("Back to Places"), which a press leaves focus in the words. While the words have focus the composer’s frame shows the focus ring, in every form, and the words draw none of their own; without `onChange` the words are text and take no focus.

components.name: MangaPage
components.title: MangaPage
components.summary: MangaPage draws one page of an issue at its trim (1448 × 2048): its art once drawn, or its layout's frames before.
components.use: one page of an issue at its trim: its art once drawn, its layout's frames before, or blank when it is not made yet, with a selection only on the editor's canvas.

instead.when: the issue's pages as the reader turns them
every page with its stage at once
an issue on a shelf

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable; read as one image named by `label`, `alt` or `title` (else "Page"), followed by "selected", how many frames are drawing or waiting, the area to redraw (`maskLabel`) and the item selected (`selectionLabel`), and with `title` or `meta` it sits in a figure captioned by them, where the `action` slot takes focus.

components.name: IssueStrip
components.title: IssueStrip
components.summary: IssueStrip shows the issue as the reader turns it: the cover alone, then the content pages paired into spreads, with a rule at every page turn.
components.use: the issue as the reader turns it, in Layout and under the editor's canvas: the cover alone, then the pages in spreads with a rule at every page turn.

instead.when: Proof, every page with how far it has come
one page on its own
a page's panels, lettering and sound effects
an issue on a shelf

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable; its label (default "The issue, spread by spread") and key read as text, then a list named "Spreads", each spread a list item holding its pages as images (named by `label` or `alt`, else "Page", with "selected"), the one `selectSpread` rings starting with "Selected spread", and the page-turn rules hidden.

components.name: PageWall
components.title: PageWall
components.summary: PageWall is Proof: every page of the issue at once, in spreads, each with its caption and how far it has come.
components.use: the Proof view: every page of the issue at once in spreads, each with its caption and how far it has come (Laid out, Drawn, Lettered, Proofed).

instead.when: placing a page in its issue while editing
editing a page
one page on its own

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable; a list named by `label` (default "The whole issue") with a spread per item: each page is an image named by its `label`, `alt` or `title`, then its title, meta and stage (an image named by its step) read as text, with a "Page turn" separator between spreads.

components.name: LayerStrip
components.title: LayerStrip
components.summary: LayerStrip lists a page's layers by kind, in reading order, under the editor's canvas: panels, lettering, sound effects.
components.use: a page's layers under the editor's canvas: panels, lettering and sound effects, a track per kind in reading order, with the issue strip on top.

instead.when: a cut's tracks in time
the issue's spreads on their own
who or what a panel holds

accessibility_declared.design: Each track reads its name and count, then its layers: with `onSelect`, a listbox named by the track and one Tab stop, where Left and Right move between layers, Enter, Space or a click choose one, and the chosen one reads "selected"; without it, a list whose selected item reads "current". Each layer reads its number and label, with "drawn into the art" when `muted`, pictures are hidden, and an empty track reads "None yet".

components.name: MentionChip
components.title: MentionChip
components.summary: MentionChip shows who or what a panel holds: a cast member (@), a place (#) or a prop, with its picture and a quiet note.
components.use: who or what a panel or a prompt holds: a cast member (@), a place (#), a reference ($) or a prop, with its picture and a quiet note such as the outfit and the emotion.

instead.when: a character's face, name and role in a row
a mention inside prose
narrowing a feed by kind
words kept as removable tags

accessibility_declared.design: Read as text, its mark first ("@Aiko", "#Harbour") then the note; with `href` it is a link that Tab reaches and Enter follows, named the same way; with `onClick` it is a button, named by `label` when given, that says whether what it opens is expanded. The picture is hidden.

components.name: Manuscript
components.title: Manuscript
components.summary: Manuscript is the script's page: its tools on top (the block type, where the cursor is), the sections, and what it reports under them (saved, length, Maki's check).
components.use: the script's page, for episodes and manga issues alike: its tools on top, the numbered sections, and what it reports under them (saved, length, Maki's check).

instead.when: one numbered section
a scene read as cuts
Studio's prompt
a long text in a form

accessibility_declared.design: A region named by `label` (default "Script"); its toolbar, sections and footer read and take focus in order. While the body scrolls it is itself a Tab stop, a group named "Scenes", so the arrows and Page Up and Page Down scroll it (axe: a scrolling region must be reachable by keyboard); it shows the focus ring inside its edge. When everything fits it is no stop at all.

components.name: ManuscriptSection
components.title: ManuscriptSection
components.summary: ManuscriptSection is one numbered section of a scene note or an imported script: #number, title (or a slugline with `slug`), the prose, the word count.
components.use: one numbered section of a scene note or an imported script: its number, title or slugline, the prose and the word count, with what was found in it in the margin.

instead.when: one block of a screenplay inside it
the whole page with its tools and status
something found in the words
a shelf's heading

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable; read as "#" and its number, the title as a level-3 heading, the prose and its word count ("240 words"), the section being written (`current`) is marked "current", and `with` reads as its line ("At the same time as #4 · Toddy's bedroom"). With `onTold` the told words are a button Tab reaches, named "How the two are told: Cut between them", with a menu popup whose choice in force is read as checked; Up and Down move through it, Enter chooses, Escape closes it and focus goes back to the words. The margin's proposals follow in reading order.

components.name: Mention
components.title: Mention
components.summary: Mention is a reference inside prose: `@` a character (filled), `#` a place (underlined), `&` an object (`kind="object"`, a hairline box, never broken across lines).
components.use: a reference inside prose or a prompt: @ a character, # a place, $ a reference the creator added, ringed while its card is open.

instead.when: who or what a panel or a prompt binds, with its picture and note
a quiet action inside a line of text
words a check flagged inside a sentence

accessibility_declared.design: Not focusable; read as text, its mark first ("@Aiko", "#Harbour", "&The red watch"), an event as its quoted title and where it was told, the picture and glyph hidden, with "missing" after a `missing` one and "card open" after the `active` one.

components.name: ProposalCard
components.title: ProposalCard
components.summary: ProposalCard is one event, change or link found in writing, waiting for the person.
components.use: one event, change or link found in writing, waiting for the person beside the words it came from: stated, inferred, or a conflict with its Ask Maki.

instead.when: something Maki proposes inside the chat
a change shown in place in the words
a check pinned to a cut on a sheet

accessibility_declared.design: Read as text: the title, "conflict" on a conflict, the note and "Inferred" on an inferred find, with the picture hidden; the `action` slot takes focus. With `accepted` set, Tab reaches the "Accept" toggle button, "pressed" when accepted, which runs `onAccept`.

components.name: SpendButton
components.title: SpendButton
components.summary: An action that spends fragments: Sakuga's `Button` with AniCanon's price after the label: the fragment mark and the amount, in regular weight and the muted ink, part of the one action with no rule between them.
components.use: an action that spends fragments: Generate, Draw it again, Make the clip, Plan scene 5.

instead.when: an action that costs nothing
a fragment amount inside a sentence
a price on a choice card

accessibility_declared.design: Button's own: a native button (a link with `href`), so Tab reaches it, Enter activates it, and Space does too on a button. A screen reader hears its label, then the price as "~100 fragments"; the mark and icons are hidden. With `href` and `disabled` it is a disabled button, out of the tab order, so a price can't be spent through a disabled link. While `busy` it stays focusable and a second press can't spend twice; a screen reader hears `busyLabel` once.

components.name: SpendTiles
components.title: SpendTiles
components.summary: `OptionTiles` whose large cards carry fragments: an option's `amount` (what a pack or plan gives, the card's headline) and `cost` (what choosing it charges, under its description), each with the fragment mark.
components.use: a choice whose cards carry fragments: the Fragments packs and plans, and the first choice of a flow when each way costs something different.

instead.when: a choice that costs nothing
the action that spends them

accessibility_declared.design: OptionTiles' own: with one choice the cards are a radio group, one Tab stop that the arrows move through. A screen reader hears each card's name, the amount or cost as "24,990 fragments", the description and the footnote; the mark and art are hidden.

components.name: Cropper
components.title: Cropper
components.summary: A crop of a picture: a circle, a square or a box of the shot's own shape, moved over the whole picture.
components.use: to choose the part of a picture that is kept: an avatar from a face sheet or a variant, a logo's square.

instead.when: showing a picture already cut
choosing among whole pictures
a file being added

accessibility_declared.design: An application named by `label`, described by `hint`, and one Tab stop. The arrows move the circle a tenth of its width, and with Shift a whole width. + and − zoom (not at a fixed size), 1 to 9 jump to a region's centre, and Home goes to the first. When a move, a zoom or a jump ends, the page's live region says where it is ("Face 3 of 6, zoom 1.3 times", or "Face 3 of 6" at a fixed size); a drag is never spoken while it runs. The slider, when there is one, is a named slider, and − and + are buttons. In forced colours the circle and its handle keep a Highlight ring.

components.name: VideoPlayer
components.title: VideoPlayer
components.summary: VideoPlayer is a clip played where it is shown: its picture, with play, the track, sound and full screen over it.
components.use: a clip that plays where it is shown: a Library item, a landed take on Studio's stage.

instead.when: the frame being edited, with its guides
a clip in a grid or a strip
only the playhead under a picture
hearing a voice line or a take's sound

accessibility_declared.design: A group named "{name}, video". Tab reaches play or pause (a button named "Play {name}", "Pause {name}" or "Play {name} again"), the seek slider ("Seek in {name}", a second per arrow), mute (a toggle, "Mute {name}") and full screen (a toggle, "Full screen"). With focus anywhere in the player, Space or K plays and pauses, M mutes, F goes full screen and Left and Right step a second; keyboard focus inside keeps the controls shown (a pointer's focus lets them fade), and the large play and the picture's press do what play does; the large play goes as it plays, and hands its focus to play or pause. The loader is named "Loading {name}". Gap: the time is read through the slider only, with no live update while it plays.

components.name: MakiFinding
components.title: MakiFinding
components.summary: MakiFinding is one thing Maki's Review found, as a line of her reply: a small mark, what doesn't hold up and why, and every event it is in.
components.use: one thing Maki's Review found, inside a `MakiFindingGroup` in her reply.

instead.when: something Maki proposes inside a reply
something found in writing, beside the words it came from
a check pinned to work on a sheet

accessibility_declared.design: An item of its group's list, named by its title. A line that opens is one button, read as its severity, "Show {title} on the map" and its note, expanded or collapsed; the mark is hidden. Open, its events are a list named "In 3 events", then Ask Maki and Keep on purpose take focus. A kept one reads "Kept on purpose by {name} · {date}", or "Kept on purpose" with no one named, and its reason, then Reopen.

components.name: SidePanel
components.title: SidePanel
components.summary: SidePanel is the one container for a side area beside a view: an event, a character, a place, Maki.
components.use: any side area beside a view: an event, a character or a place on Story, Maki's chat.

instead.when: a dialog over the view
a panel that slides up on a phone
a boxed group of settings inside a page

accessibility_declared.design: A section named by `label`. The body is a region Tab reaches when its `role` is `region`, or a log when it is a conversation, which Tab also reaches so it scrolls from the keyboard, held back while `busy`; "Jump to the latest" is a button.

components.name: MakiFindingGroup
components.title: MakiFindingGroup
components.summary: MakiFindingGroup is one group of what Review found, inside Maki's reply: its label and count ("Conflicts · 2"), an optional quiet note, then its `MakiFinding`s.
components.use: to group Review's findings inside Maki's reply.

instead.when: a section of a side area
a section of a page

accessibility_declared.design: Its findings are a list named by its label.

components.name: MakiStep
components.title: MakiStep
components.summary: MakiStep is one line of what Maki is doing or did, at the top of her reply: "Read the story · 26 events".
components.use: what Maki did before she answered, at the top of a `MakiTurn`.

instead.when: Maki's answer itself
a job running elsewhere

accessibility_declared.design: Read as text; a step that opens is a button, expanded or collapsed. A running step's loader says its label once.

components.name: MakiSuggestions
components.title: MakiSuggestions
components.summary: MakiSuggestions is what to ask Maki first, as rows that send on a press, phrased as the person would type them.
components.use: the first things to ask, when nothing has been said yet in `MakiPanel`.

instead.when: an answer Maki asks for
a filter or a toggle

accessibility_declared.design: A list named "What to ask"; each row is a button that sends its words.

components.name: ScreenplayEditor
components.title: ScreenplayEditor
components.summary: ScreenplayEditor is a scene written on the page: each block is a `ScreenplayLine` of its kind, typed in place, with no box around the words.
components.use: to write a scene of a script on the page, inside a `ManuscriptSection`, the blocks typed as screenplay lines.

instead.when: a scene that only reads
the prompt that makes a take
a plain multi-line field

accessibility_declared.design: A group named by `label` (default "Script") and described by its keys ("Enter starts the next block, … Escape, then Tab, leaves the script"). Each block is a textbox named by its kind ("Scene heading", "Action", "Character", "Parenthetical", "Dialogue", "Transition"), multi-line for action and dialogue, one Tab stop for the whole script (the block last written in). A change of kind is said in a polite live region. The mention list is a listbox the line controls, its active option the line's active descendant.

components.name: Contents
components.title: Contents
components.summary: Contents lists a document's sections in order, one press each: the sections of an open canon document under its row.
components.use: the sections of one document, in order, where one is open beside them: a canon document's sections under its row.

instead.when: a page's main sections
rows with a picture, a second line or an action
a link inside a sentence
the views inside a production

accessibility_declared.design: A navigation named by `label` ("Sections of World rules") holding an ordered list, so a screen reader says how many sections there are. Each section is a link or a button Tab reaches, and the open one is marked current. "6 more" is a button; pressing it puts focus on the first section it opened. In forced colours the open section is drawn in Highlight and focus keeps its ring.
